prompt:
The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

The profile below describes the positional priorities of the British electorate.

<profile>
  tan: 0.60
  gal: 0.40
</profile>

Below are two texts.

TEXT_C:
The Green Party’s message is urgent and hopeful: in dark days of Brexit turmoil, a failing democracy and accelerating climate breakdown, the next decade is decisive. If not now, when?

Their programme is a Green New Deal to deliver both climate safety and social justice. Investing over £100 billion a year (with additional UBI funding), it puts the UK on track for net-zero by 2030 while lifting everyone up. Power and wealth are to be shared more fairly; wellbeing will replace GDP as the yardstick of progress; and no community will be left behind.

Key Green New Deal pillars:
- Energy: Replace fossil fuels with renewables; community energy; end subsidies to oil and gas; a rising Carbon Tax to render fossil fuels unviable; no fracking, no new nuclear; expand grids, storage and interconnectors.
- Housing: Insulate every home; deep retrofit 1 million buildings a year; roll out home renewables; replace gas heating; 100,000 new Passivhaus-standard council homes annually; higher standards for all new builds; protect renters and end fuel poverty.
- Transport: Make public transport cheaper than driving; electrify rail; reopen lines and expand freight by rail; empower councils to run buses and trams; build safe cycleways/footpaths; Frequent Flyer Levy; stop new runways and road-building; end sales of new petrol/diesel vehicles by 2030 with widespread EV charging.
- Industry: A circular economy with right-to-repair, ten-year warranties and bans on single-use plastics; grants and standards to decarbonise heavy industry; skills and apprenticeships; regional mutual banks; CCS for steel/cement.
- Food, farming & forestry: A ten‑year transition to agroecology; rewilding and urban greening; 700 million trees; cut pesticides; a right to food; support “less but better” meat and a fair farmer-led transition.

To make it happen, Greens will:
- Remain and reform the EU via a People’s Vote, using Europe to drive climate action, social rights, fair taxation and humane refugee policy while safeguarding freedom of movement.
- Grow democracy: proportional representation; votes at 16; an elected second chamber; citizens’ assemblies and a People’s Constitution; curb oligarchic media power; a Digital Bill of Rights; devolve power and resources to councils; a Carbon Chancellor and a Future Generations Act.

Quality of Life Guarantee: reverse austerity; invest in the NHS (+£6bn/yr) and end privatisation; expand mental and reproductive health; boost schools (+£4bn/yr); scrap tuition fees; smaller classes; restore arts and climate/nature education. Deliver secure incomes and homes with a Universal Basic Income (no one worse off), a £12 Living Wage, 35 hours free childcare from 9 months, gig worker rights, rent controls and an end to no‑fault evictions.

Justice and rights: dismantle the hostile environment; humane migration and Windrush justice; tackle discrimination and misogyny; LGBTIQA+ and disability rights; halve the prison population through prevention and restorative justice; end the war on drugs with legal, regulated supply and health-led support.

Nature and animals: a Clean Air Act; ecocide law; right to roam; more protected land and seas; end factory farming, live exports and hunting; recognise animal sentience.

Global justice: aid to 1% of GNI, climate finance and technology transfer; fair trade rules; end arms sales; a peace-first foreign policy.

Paying for it: simplify and toughen taxes on wealth and corporate profits; introduce a Land Value Tax; a rising Carbon Tax; crack down on avoidance; cancel wasteful projects (Trident, HS2, airport expansion, new roads); and borrow for productive green investment while catalysing private capital.

The Greens say they’ve been on the right side of history—and will get the future right. Every Green vote is a vote to make the Green New Deal real.

TEXT_F:
Labour’s 2019 manifesto promises real change: a fair, green, democratic economy that puts wealth and power in the hands of the many, not the few, while reversing a decade of Conservative failure on living standards, public services, climate, and Brexit.

- Mission and values: Rewrite the rules of the economy so it works for everyone; take on vested interests, polluters, and tax-dodgers; tackle poverty and inequality; guarantee universal, high‑quality public services funded fairly.

- Green Industrial Revolution: Deliver most emissions cuts by 2030; create 1 million good, unionised climate jobs; invest through a £400bn National Transformation Fund (including a £250bn Green Transformation Fund) plus a National Investment Bank and regional banks; delist climate‑wrecking firms; decentralise power and investment.

- Energy and ownership: 90% of electricity and 50% of heat from low‑carbon by 2030; ban fracking; mass home retrofit; expand wind, solar, tidal, storage, grids and heat networks; public ownership of energy, water, rail and mail to end rip‑offs and reinvest surpluses.

- Transport: Publicly owned, integrated rail with electrification and HS2 to Scotland; Crossrail for the North; better freight, cycling and walking; empower councils to own/regulate buses and restore routes; free bus travel for under‑25s where councils take control; accelerate EV transition and charging; aim to end new combustion car sales by 2030.

- Environment and food: Clean Air Act, flood defence boost, nature restoration, stronger protections; Right to Food, halve food bank use in a year and end need in three; net‑zero food by 2040; producer responsibility and recycling; end cruel wildlife practices.

- Fair funding and tax: Restore public services with a £150bn Social Transformation Fund; crack down on avoidance; reverse some corporation tax cuts; raise income tax only above £80,000; no VAT rise; insource services and end PFI.

- NHS and care: 4.3% average annual health funding rise; end privatisation; free prescriptions and basic dentistry; expand mental health and public health; build a National Care Service with free personal care and ethical provision.

- Education: National Education Service with free lifelong learning; restore Sure Start (Sure Start Plus), 30 hours free preschool for 2–4s; properly fund schools, end SATs, Arts Premium, enrich curriculum; bring academies/free schools under local democratic control; abolish tuition fees and restore maintenance grants.

- Work and rights: Real Living Wage of at least £10 for all; sectoral collective bargaining; day‑one rights; end zero‑hours; strengthen unions; move toward a 32‑hour week within a decade with no loss of pay; enforce via a new Workers’ Protection Agency; Inclusive Ownership Funds for workers; UBI pilots.

- Social security and equality: Replace DWP with a supportive Department for Social Security; scrap Universal Credit and punitive sanctions; lift disabled and carers’ support; uphold women’s, BAME, disabled and LGBT+ rights with stronger enforcement and a new Department for Women and Equalities.

- Housing: Build over 1 million social homes in a decade (100,000 council homes a year by end of Parliament); end Right to Buy; renters’ rights with rent controls, open‑ended tenancies and national licensing; leasehold abolition; end rough sleeping in five years.

- Policing and justice: Rebuild neighbourhood policing; tackle institutional bias; restore legal aid, probation in public hands, and invest in prevention; humane borders, end the hostile environment and indefinite detention; safe routes for refugees.

- Democracy: Abolish the House of Lords for an elected Senate via a Constitutional Convention; extend the vote to 16; automatic voter registration; curb dark money and lobbying.

- Brexit: Final‑say referendum within six months, with a credible leave deal that protects jobs, rights and peace, versus remain; implement the people’s decision.

- Internationalism and defence: Put peace, human rights and climate at the core; War Powers Act; suspend arms sales used to violate rights (e.g. in Yemen) and recognise Palestine; maintain NATO, renew Trident while pursuing multilateral disarmament; restore UK climate leadership and 0.7% aid focused on justice.

It’s time for real change—for the many, not the few.

Judge whether TEXT_C or TEXT_F aligns more closely with this profile.
